subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-297.draft.md
discipline: Refute, do not confirm. A recording entry earns CONSENT only if every assertion it makes is re-derivable from bytes this review resolved itself. Three centres of gravity. First, the entry is the third member of a lineage whose two predecessors were both dual-REJECTed, so the lineage sentences were treated as the likeliest site of drift and were tested by executing the repairs rather than reading the claims: the freeze pin was counted across v1/v2/v3 and the v15 quotation was compared by == against the live contract at each version, which is the only way to decide WHERE a finding landed. Second, every number and token the entry carries forward (HEAD, COORD digest, file-08 digest, the DR-122 status token, required-now, condition 2, condition 4, the no-cell-edit branch endpoints) was resolved from its own source rather than from the review prompt that supplied it, because a prompt-supplied number and a live number agreeing is a measurement, not an assumption. Third, all 28 of the frozen successor's pinned inputs were re-hashed from disk, so the ACCEPT this entry records rests on a closure this review re-measured rather than inherited. The attacks are listed with their outcomes, including the three that looked most promising and failed.

attackResults.attack: The strongest available refutation: show that the draft's lineage sentence 'sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v1 ... its findings landed at sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v2' is contradicted by the frozen bytes. The frozen v3's own purpose field appears to say the opposite - it says v3 lands the Codex Stage A sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v1 SHOULD-FIX and the Claude Stage A sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v1 SHOULD-FIX IR-FCOUTFAIL-G1-S1 - and Claude's Stage A discipline text describes v3 as landing three SHOULD-FIXes, two of them raised against golden.v1. On that reading the v1 findings landed at v3, not v2, and the draft's two-step lineage would be false.
attackResults.method: Refused to settle it on purpose prose in either direction and measured where each repair physically landed. Counted IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md occurrences across the three versions, and compared quotedV15OwnerOfValues at each version by == against the live sarif-projection-contract.v15 $.requiredOutputFailure.ownerOfValues.
attackResults.result: REFUTED, and the draft is right. The freeze pin count is v1=2, v2=7, v3=7 - the Codex v1 required repair landed at v2 and merely persists at v3. The v15 quotation reads 'd9-exit-contract.v1.14 already records this golden...' at v1 (the broken quotation IR-FCOUTFAIL-G1-S1 names) and 'D9 v1.14 already records this golden...' at both v2 and v3, byte-exact against the live v15 - so the Claude v1 required repair also landed at v2. What v2 got wrong was only the attribution: its purpose credited both findings to 'golden.v2 Stage A' reviews that did not exist, which is precisely what Claude's IR-FCOUTFAIL-G2-S1 and the Codex v2 SHOULD-FIX ('The purpose assigns both predecessor findings to nonexistent golden.v2 Stage A reviews', requiredRepair 'In purpose, attribute both findings to Stage A sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v1') caught. v3's purpose therefore names golden.v1 not because the repairs are landing late, but because that sentence IS the v2 repair. The draft's two-step chain - v1 findings landed at v2, v2 findings landed at v3 - is the only reading consistent with the bytes.

advisories.title: The entry says 'fixture implementations' in the plural while exactly one fixture file is authored, for exactly one namedCase.
advisories.measurement: The heading reads 'FC-OUTFAIL no-committed-run fixture implementations' and the Subject paragraph reads 'fixture implementations for the FC-OUTFAIL.no-committed-run namedCase', both plural against a singular namedCase. The frozen artifact's own whatIsAuthored reads 'One catalog member. One fixture file.', authoredCatalog.members has length 1, and the fixtures directory holds a single file. The D-296 analogue used the same plural phrase and authored two files, where the plural was literally true: sarif-fc-nonauth-term.v1 holds FC-NONAUTH-TERM.renderer-chosen-d9-refuse.json and FC-NONAUTH-TERM.rewritten-hosttermination-refuse.json.
whyNotShouldFix: No asserted value is false. The same paragraph names the single authored fixture by exact path and states that FC-OUTFAIL.committed-run-preserved stays NOT-AUTHORED, so the count is disclosed in the entry's own bytes three sentences from the heading. A reader cannot be left believing two files exist.

The plural reads correctly at obligation level. The entry dispositions both namedCases of OBL-FC-OUTFAIL-FX - one AUTHORED, one NOT-AUTHORED - and 'fixture implementations' is the obligation-level noun for that work, not a file count.

It is recorder-blessed convention rather than novelty in this subject. D-296 carries the identical phrase at this same HEAD and was adopted after dual review. Raising it here would reject a form the register already accepted, on a successor whose purpose is to land unrelated findings.
The heading is in fact more specific than the accepted D-296 form, since it names the single namedCase that the plural covers.
advisories.ifEverRepaired: A later entry in this lineage could scope the noun to the count, for instance 'fixture implementation' where one namedCase is authored. This is not a repair this entry owes and this advisory must not be read as requiring a turn-2 draft.

advisories.title: The OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX sentence anchors its remasurement bound to D-296 where D-297 would be the tighter bound.
advisories.measurement: The Decision reads 'leftover-design of OBL-FC-NONAUTH-TERM-FX remains on leftover-join.v4 until a later leftover-join remasurement after D-296.' The parallel sentence in adopted D-296 carried no anchor at all: 'until a later leftover-join remasurement.' Since this entry is D-297, the tightest true bound is 'after D-297'; 'after D-296' is a strictly weaker window whose open end includes the interval between the two entries.
whyNotShouldFix: The statement is true as written. The last live heading is D-296, leftover-join.v4 is the current DR-122 leftover-join at draft time, and no remasurement landed between D-296 and this draft, so the weaker bound admits nothing that actually occurred.
The entry states 'Does not remasure leftover-join.v4' separately and unconditionally, so the currency of leftover-join.v4 after this recording does not rest on the anchor.
The looseness is a bound-tightness question, not a false measurement, and it resolves the moment this entry is adopted as D-297.
advisories.ifEverRepaired: A later entry could anchor to its own number, or drop the anchor as D-296 did. Not owed here.
